data.cultural_impact: The name Demas carries a pleasant and affectionate meaning, attributed to Greek mythology. Its association with love and affection would have been cherished by the people of ancient Greece and later by the early Christians who bore this name. Demas is a reflection of the deep human desire to be loved, appreciated, and cherished. In the Christian context, Demas’ name may have served as a source of encouragement and comfort for those who carried this name. They were likely revered and loved by their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Demas is a name deeply rooted in biblical history. In the New Testament, Demas is mentioned as a "coworker" and "fellow-labourer" of the Apostle Paul. This association with Paul, one of the greatest early Christian leaders, implies that Demas was a devout and committed man of faith. As a follower of Christ, Demas' name carries spiritual significance as a reminder of the importance of working in partnership and unity with others to spread the gospel, and of being a faithful servant to God. The name Demas also serves as a testament to the enduring love and support of the early Christian community, imbuing those who bear the name with a sense of belonging, identity, and spiritual connection to their heritage.

historical_references.context: Demas is mentioned in the New Testament as a companion of Paul and Barnabas, but later he is described as having forsaken Paul.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Demas continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Demas is believed to represent a person who is zealous and devoted in their faith at first, but later falls from grace due to worldly desires and distractions. In the New Testament, Demas is mentioned as a companion of Paul who loved worldly pleasures and abandoned the apostle in his final days. (2 Timothy 4:10)
